name: sqlite_snapshot
description: Copy a SQLite database with its write-ahead log, shared-memory file and rollback journal into a NEW private directory and apply the WAL in the copy, so the state SQLite itself would show can be queried while the evidence is never touched or written beside. Every file of the set (database, -wal, -shm, -journal) is streamed once, through sha256, into original/ (new files, 0600, the source's size and time read before and after: changed_during_copy says a live file moved under the copy; the files are copied one after another, not at one instant, and the answer says so). The WAL is read from the copy against the format (header magic, version, page size, its own checksum, then each frame's salts and cumulative checksum in the byte order the magic gives) and reports frames in the file, frames valid, frames committed (the last commit), valid frames after it that no commit covers (never applied), and the first invalid frame with its reason (a leftover of an earlier generation, a damaged or torn frame, a file that ends inside a frame). It is applied by SQLite itself to a second copy (applied/database.sqlite: the copy and its -wal opened and checkpointed; the -shm is not used): the frame count SQLite reports is compared with this tool's reading and a difference is said, and the pages of the main file the WAL changed are counted. A WAL with no valid header, no committed frame or another page size is not applied and the answer says why (then `database` is the copy of the main file). A rollback journal is copied and reported (hot header or not) and is NOT rolled back. Give `database` (or the snapshot directory) to sqlite_query as db_path. Not measured: deleted records, the freelist and unallocated pages are neither read nor recovered; a frame after the last commit is reported, not applied; whether a live set was consistent when copied is not established; a database encrypted by an extension (SQLCipher) is refused with its first bytes and their entropy, which identifies nothing. Exit 0 with status partial when the copy was made and the WAL could not be applied or read; the copy of an unreadable set is exit 1. Nothing is overwritten: an existing out_dir is refused.

db_path.description: The SQLite database file. Its -wal, -shm and -journal beside it (named from the real path, as SQLite looks for them) are copied too.

out_dir.description: New directory for the snapshot (default: a new sqlite_snapshot-<id> directory). It must not exist. In a job it must lie under $OUT: give {OUT}/<name>.

apply_wal.description: Apply the WAL in a second copy (default true). False copies the set and reads the WAL and applies nothing.

max_bytes.description: Largest set to copy, in bytes (default 8 GiB, at most 1 TiB); a bigger set is refused before anything is copied.

max_seconds.description: Time budget in seconds (default 600, at most 1700); it ends the copy and the WAL check (a WAL check cut short is said).

quick_check.description: Run PRAGMA quick_check on the applied copy and return its first 20 lines (default false; it reads the whole database).
